These constants are approximations, and published values for the same modality differ substantially across studies and stimulus conditions. What is stable, and what the exam tests, is the ordering — weight and vision fine, taste and smell coarse — together with the proportionality itself.

visual.title: One chain, five front ends, three adaptation profiles
visual.alt: A five-step chain from stimulus through channel opening to a graded receptor potential, all-or-none action potentials and rate coding of intensity; a table of the transduction mechanism for touch, hearing, vision, smell, taste and temperature or pain, marking vision as the case where channels close and the cell hyperpolarises; and three cards contrasting rapidly adapting receptors, slowly adapting receptors and nociceptors, which sensitise instead of adapting.
visual.caption: Rapidly adapting receptors report that something changed; slowly adapting ones report that it is still there. Nociceptors do neither — they get louder.
